vectors.name: oml-grammar/reserved/nan-bare-is-a-number-token-not-a-label
vectors.comment: `nan` is claimed by the reserved-float-spelling tokenizer rule (rule 7) before IDENT is reached, so it never reaches label position at all -- the failure is a token-level mismatch, not the reserved-word-label error nan/inf never get.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/reserved/quoted-nan-is-an-ordinary-label
vectors.comment: Quoting routes `nan` to the STRING tokenizer rule (rule 1) instead of the reserved float spelling, so it is a perfectly ordinary label here.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/reserved/null-bare-label-at-top-level-fails-on-trailing-colon
vectors.comment: The sharp edge in Sec4.6.1: `null` fails the edge-vs-scalar lookahead test (it IS null/true/false), so the parser takes the scalar branch, consumes `null`, and then fails on the leftover `:` as trailing content -- NOT the reserved-word-label error. Distinguishing these two by code is exactly what Sec4.6.1 says conformance vectors must do.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/reserved/null-bare-label-inside-a-node-is-the-reserved-word-error
vectors.comment: Inside a node, label position is unambiguous (no top-level scalar-or-edge lookahead applies), so this is the specific reserved-word-label error rather than a trailing-content error -- the companion case to the top-level vector above.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/arrays/repeated-label-sugar-expands-in-place
vectors.comment: [1,2,3] expands at parse time into three repeated `b` edges -- indistinguishable from writing `b: 1; b: 2; b: 3` directly. An array is not a value in the Document model.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/arrays/empty-array-is-an-error-not-a-zero-edge-expansion
vectors.comment: An empty array and an absent label are the same Document, and OML deliberately does not offer two spellings for one thing.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/arrays/nested-array-is-rejected
vectors.comment: An array element that is itself an array has nothing to nest into -- the Document model has no bare nested list (Sec2.2.3).

vectors.name: oml-grammar/arrays/newline-inside-array-is-an-error
vectors.comment: Comma is the only element separator inside [...]. A newline immediately after a real comma is legal and purely decorative (Sec4.3.1's fourth rule: separators and comments are otherwise insignificant inside [...]) -- this vector's original input mistakenly had a comma present ("b: [1,\n2, 3]\n"), which never exercised the illegal case its name claimed and was correctly flagged by the omnist-py session (omnist#284, closed not-a-bug) before implementation. This corrected input has NO comma between 1 and 2, so the newline is the only thing standing in for a separator, which is exactly the illegal case. Confirmed live: fails at line 2, col 1 with 'expected , or ] in array'.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/strings/raw-string-performs-no-escape-processing
vectors.comment: Raw strings (Extended, read-only) perform no escape processing at all -- a backslash inside is a literal backslash, unlike the double-quoted Core form.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/strings/multiline-string-strips-leading-newline
vectors.comment: The optional newline immediately after the opening """ is consumed and is not part of the value.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/strings/multiline-string-closes-at-first-run-of-three-quotes
vectors.comment: A run of one or two quotes inside a multiline string is literal content; the string only closes at a run of three or more, and only the first three of that run are consumed as the terminator.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/date-then-time-lookahead-yields-one-datetime-token
vectors.comment: At a position where DATE matches, the tokenizer checks whether the next character is T followed by a TIME-shaped lookahead; here it is, so DATETIME is emitted as one token rather than DATE followed by a separate value.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/date-then-non-time-suffix-is-date-plus-trailing-content
vectors.comment: The lookahead after DATE fails (T99 does not match TIME), so DATE is emitted alone and whatever follows -- the bare identifier T99 -- is tokenized independently, then rejected as trailing content once the single-value position is already filled.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/shape/single-top-level-scalar-is-the-whole-document
vectors.comment: One of the three legal top-level shapes: the document IS that one leaf, with no wrapper.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/errors/bare-word-in-value-position-is-an-error
vectors.comment: A bare identifier that is not null/true/false is not a string -- OML has no implicit string-from-identifier coercion anywhere.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/errors/literal-control-character-in-string-is-an-error
vectors.comment: A literal control character below U+0020 -- here a raw newline before the closing quote -- is an error in a double-quoted (Core) string.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/errors/unrecognized-escape-is-an-error
vectors.comment: Recognized escapes are exactly \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t and \uXXXX; \q is none of these.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/errors/unpaired-high-surrogate-is-an-error
vectors.comment: A \uXXXX in the high-surrogate range D800-DBFF MUST be immediately followed by a second \uXXXX in the low-surrogate range DC00-DFFF; this one has no partner.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/errors/unterminated-string-is-an-error
vectors.comment: End of input reached with the string still open -- no closing quote.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/numbers/leading-zero-integer-is-an-error
vectors.comment: int-part only permits a single 0, or a nonzero digit followed by more digits -- never a 0 followed by more digits. This closes previously-undefined behavior: nothing in this spec constrained NUMBER/INTEGER lexically before Sec4.2.3 existed.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/numbers/leading-zero-in-decimal-is-an-error
vectors.comment: The leading-zero restriction on int-part applies identically whether the literal ends up tokenized as INTEGER or NUMBER -- a fractional part does not exempt the integer part from the same rule.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/numbers/single-zero-and-negative-forms-are-valid
vectors.comment: A bare 0 is exactly one digit, so it's never a leading zero; a fraction less than 1 legitimately starts with 0.; a negative sign does not change int-part's own leading-zero rule since it applies after the optional minus.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/date-with-out-of-range-month-is-an-error
vectors.comment: ABNF's 2DIGIT for the month component permits 00-99; only 01-12 are calendar-valid, and that range check is normative even though ABNF cannot express it.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/date-with-day-invalid-for-month-is-an-error
vectors.comment: February never has a 30th day regardless of leap year, distinguishing this from the leap-year-specific case below.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/february-29-in-a-non-leap-year-is-an-error
vectors.comment: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not 400, so it is not a leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar -- distinct from 2000-02-29 (the happy-path vector below), which is.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/february-29-in-a-leap-year-is-valid
vectors.comment: 2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year -- the one case the div-by-100 exception itself has an exception for.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/leap-second-is-an-error
vectors.comment: OML has no leap-second spelling; second is 00-59 with no exception, unlike ISO 8601 which permits 60 in some contexts.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/tz-offset-minute-out-of-range-is-an-error
vectors.comment: tz-offset MUST use the same minute range as TIME (00-59), not a wider one. This is the case that surfaced the gap: an implementation that validates tz-offset via a separate code path from TIME can end up normalizing +00:60 to a 1-hour offset instead of rejecting it, silently colliding it with a document that legitimately wrote +01:00 -- confirmed live against a pre-fix reference implementation. The offset MUST be rejected outright, not normalized.

vectors.name: oml-grammar/temporals/tz-offset-within-range-is-valid
vectors.comment: A legitimate, in-range offset (e.g. India Standard Time) parses normally -- confirms the tz-offset fix in the vector above doesn't reject valid input, only out-of-range minutes. The expected value's seconds are canonicalized to :00 even though the source text omits them, matching every sibling OML-datetime vector's own convention (see date-then-time-lookahead-yields-one-datetime-token above) -- a temporal-scalar value in a parse vector MUST already be in the format's own canonical spelling, not just any value that happens to compare semantically equal, since a string-backed implementation (rather than one with a native temporal type) compares literally. Was originally un-canonicalized here; found and reported as omnist-spec#51 by the Rust port during omnist-rs#165.
